correctness.rationale: One outer cycle is the polynomial \(p(\lambda)=1-\alpha+\alpha(1-\eta\lambda)^k\). For even \(k\), the lower stability inequality is automatic and the upper one is exactly \(|1-\eta\lambda|<1\), giving \(\eta L<2\); for odd \(k\), the upper inequality is automatic and the lower gives the stated real-root ceiling, with multipliers \(+1\) and \(-1\) at the respective boundaries. For the minimax problem, even powers are nonnegative, so interpolation can only move modal factors toward one and cannot beat the classical equioscillating step. For odd powers the endpoint values are monotone in curvature; before the equioscillation point \(\alpha=1\) is optimal, while after it balancing endpoints yields \(F(x)=(b-a)/(2-a-b)\). The displayed auxiliary function has nonnegative derivative because \(|1-\kappa x|\ge|1-x|\) and \(\kappa(1-Q)\ge1+Q\), proving \(F\ge Q\). Equality is unique for \(k\ge2\). The verifier checks boundary multipliers, exact optimum values and dense grids as transcription guards.

value.rationale: The theorem sharply separates stability enlargement from worst-case acceleration: odd synchronization lengths can stabilize learning rates beyond the inner GD limit, yet no fixed interpolation improves the best robust spectral contraction. This directly clarifies a central motivation of Lookahead on a canonical model.

final_claim: For deterministic Lookahead with plain gradient descent on an SPD quadratic, the exact universal fixed-parameter stability boundary is \(\eta L<2\) for even \(k\) and \(\eta L<1+(2/\alpha-1)^{1/k}\) for odd \(k\); nevertheless the minimax contraction over a known spectral interval is exactly \(((\kappa-1)/(\kappa+1))^k\), uniquely attained for \(k\ge2\) by \(\eta=2/(L+\mu)\) and \(\alpha=1\).
limitations: Deterministic SPD quadratics, plain gradient-descent inner optimizer, and fixed global \(\eta,\alpha\) only.
The theorem does not address stochastic variance reduction, momentum/Adam inner states, adaptive interpolation, or nonquadratic objectives.
